title: Geometry of subgroups generated by compatible rank-one graphs
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $(G_1,T_1)$ and $(G_0,T_0)$ be split reductive affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme], with roots $\Phi_1,\Phi_0$, coroots, and simple-root bases $\Delta_1,\Delta_0$ as in [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure]. For a root $\gamma$, write $G_{i,\gamma}$ for the connected rank-one reductive subgroup containing $T_i$ and the root groups $U_{\pm\gamma}$; concretely this is the centralizer of the largest subtorus of $\ker\gamma$, as in [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections]. Root subgroups are those of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Suppose $h:T_1\to T_0$ has injective pullback on characters with finite cokernel, and $b:\Delta_1\to\Delta_0$ is a bijection. For each $\alpha\in\Delta_1$ suppose given a homomorphism $f_\alpha:G_{1,\alpha}\to G_{0,b(\alpha)}$ restricting to $h$ and mapping $U_{\pm\alpha}$ onto $U_{\pm b(\alpha)}$. Let $\Gamma_h\subset G_1\times_FG_0$ be the graph of $h$, and let $L$ be the smallest reduced closed algebraic subgroup containing $\Gamma_h$ and every graph $\Gamma_{f_\alpha}$. Here reduced means that its coordinate algebra has no nonzero nilpotents, and smallest means contained in every reduced closed algebraic subgroup containing the indicated graphs. Then $L$ exists, is smooth connected reductive, and $\Gamma_h$ is a split maximal torus of $L$. If $a=\operatorname{pr}_1|_{\Gamma_h}:\Gamma_h\xrightarrow{\sim}T_1$, the character identification $a^*:X^*(T_1)\xrightarrow{\sim}X^*(\Gamma_h)$ identifies the full root datum of $(G_1,T_1)$ with that of $(L,\Gamma_h)$, including coroots. Under this identification $a^*(\Delta_1)$ is a simple-root base, and the subgroups $\Gamma_{f_\alpha|U_{\pm\alpha}}$ are its corresponding root subgroups. If $\Delta_1=\varnothing$, then $L=\Gamma_h$.

source.place: Construction 23.17 and assertions 23.19--23.24, printed pp.490--492, including the final root-subgroup and Weyl-conjugacy paragraph completing 23.18; generation in Section 2h and 21.62. The based-root-datum assertion records the roots and coroots of the displayed rank-one graphs under the first torus projection.

proof.text: Put $S=\Gamma_h$. If $\Delta_1$ is empty, so are both root systems and $G_i=T_i$ by [lem-sfb-simple-root-generation-mixed-commutation]. The graph is a closed subgroup: on coordinate algebras its graph map is $F[T_1]\otimes_F F[T_0]\to F[T_1]$, $a\otimes b\mapsto a h^*(b)$, which is surjective since $a\otimes1\mapsto a$. Its first projection is an isomorphism. Thus $S$ is a smooth connected split torus, the smallest reduced subgroup in the statement is $S$, and the root data are identified by the first projection with empty root and coroot sets. Henceforth suppose $\Delta_1\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: 23.17, printed p.490; semisimple-rank-zero case preceding 23.14, printed p.489.

proof.text: Write $H_\alpha=\Gamma_{f_\alpha}$ and $P_\alpha^\pm=\Gamma_{f_\alpha|U_{\pm\alpha}}$. These are closed subgroup schemes isomorphic by first projection to their domains: the coordinate-algebra argument of step 1 applies also to a graph over a closed subgroup. The $H_\alpha$ are smooth and connected by [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections]. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup] to the finite disjoint union $X=S\amalg\coprod_\alpha H_\alpha$, mapped into $G_1\times G_0$, pointed at any identity. Its image is inversion-stable over every algebra, and $X$ is geometrically reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced]. Obtain the smallest closed subgroup $L$, geometrically reduced and of finite type, with the stated word-kernel construction. Each connected generating subgroup maps into the open-and-closed identity component $L^0$. Since it is reduced, it factors through $(L^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$. By [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], this is a smooth connected closed subgroup of $L$. Minimality gives $L=(L^0)_{\mathrm{red}}$. This proves existence and smooth connectedness and also proves the required minimality among reduced closed subgroups. The same construction and identity-component argument apply below to the finite families $(P_\alpha^+)$ and $(P_\alpha^-)$.

source.place: Section 2h, Propositions 2.46--2.48, printed pp.54--55; construction 23.17, printed p.490.

proof.text: First $h$ is surjective. Factor it into its faithfully flat image and a closed immersion $I\hookrightarrow T_0$ by [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization]. The subgroup $I$ is of multiplicative type. By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-character-antiduality], $X^*(T_0)\to X^*(I)$ is surjective; it is also injective, since its composite with $X^*(I)\to X^*(T_1)$ is the given injective $h^*$. Thus $I\hookrightarrow T_0$ is an isomorphism under the character anti-equivalence. Factor each $p_i:L\to G_i$ through its closed image. The first image contains $T_1,U_{\pm\alpha}$, and the second contains $T_0,U_{\pm b(\alpha)}$, using the assumptions on $f_\alpha$ and the just-proved surjectivity of $h$. The bijection $b$ and [lem-sfb-simple-root-generation-mixed-commutation] show that both images are the whole groups. Thus both projections are surjective (indeed faithfully flat), and [lem-sfb-subdirect-product-reductivity] makes $L$ reductive.

Choose Borel subgroups with bases $\Delta_i$ by [lem-sfb-simple-root-generation-mixed-commutation], and let $U_i^+,U_i^-$ be their opposite unipotent radicals. The root-product coordinates put $U_{\pm\alpha}$ and $U_{\pm b(\alpha)}$ in the corresponding radicals. Use the construction in step 2 to form the smooth connected closed subgroups $U=\langle P_\alpha^+\rangle$ and $V=\langle P_\alpha^-\rangle$. Their minimality gives $U\subseteq U_1^+\times U_0^+$ and $V\subseteq U_1^-\times U_0^-$. Both are normalized by $S$: for $s=(t,h(t))$, conjugation on a graph is the graph of conjugation by $t$, because $f_\alpha$ is a homomorphism restricting to $h$. In particular on $P_\alpha^\pm$ the character is $\pm\alpha\circ\operatorname{pr}_1|_S$, using [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Distinct $P_\alpha^+$ and $P_\beta^-$ commute because they do so in each factor by [lem-sfb-simple-root-generation-mixed-commutation] and $b$ preserves distinctness. The roots of $(G_{1,\alpha},T_1)$ are exactly $\pm\alpha$. They are weights of $T_1$ on $\operatorname{Lie}(G_{1,\alpha})\subseteq\operatorname{Lie}(G_1)$, hence lie in $\Phi_1$. The largest subtorus $T_\alpha$ of $\ker\alpha$ centralizes $G_{1,\alpha}=C_{G_1}(T_\alpha)$, so it acts trivially on that Lie algebra; a root $\beta$ trivial on $T_\alpha$ lies in $\mathbf Q\alpha$ by character antiduality, so $\beta\in\Phi_1\cap\mathbf Q\alpha=\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$ by [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections]. Conversely, by the action formula of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations], $T_\alpha$ acts on $U_{\pm\alpha}$ through $\pm\alpha$, i.e. trivially, so $U_{\pm\alpha}\subseteq G_{1,\alpha}$; by uniqueness these are its root subgroups. The same holds for $G_{0,b(\alpha)}$. Hence $G_{1,\alpha}$ has base $\{\alpha\}$, and the generation statement shows that $T_1$ and $U_{\pm\alpha}$ generate it. Transport along the graph isomorphism: $S$ and $P_\alpha^\pm$ generate $H_\alpha$. Consequently $S$ and all the $P_\alpha^\pm$ generate $L$.

source.place: Paragraph following 23.20 and 23.21, printed p.491; 21.23 and 21.41.

proof.text: For a reductive group $G$ with Borel $B=U^+\rtimes T$, [lem-sfb-bruhat-longest-cell-charts] gives the open immersion $U^+\times B\to G$, $(u,b)\mapsto un_0b$. Left translation by $n_0^{-1}$ changes its image into $U^-B$, with $U^-=n_0^{-1}U^+n_0$ the opposite radical. The Borel product decomposition therefore gives the open immersion $U^-\times T\times U^+\to G$. Apply this to both $G_i$. Multiplication $V\times S\times U\to G_1\times G_0$ is the restriction of their product open immersion to closed subgroups of its three factors. It is thus an isomorphism onto a locally closed subscheme $C=VSU$ of $L$. Apply the same construction to $G_{1,\alpha}$, whose roots are exactly $\{\alpha,-\alpha\}$ by step 4 (from [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections]); its Borel radicals equal $U_{\pm\alpha}$ by the root-product coordinates. Transport along its graph isomorphism: $P_\alpha^- S P_\alpha^+$ is open dense in $H_\alpha$. Only density, not equality with $H_\alpha$, is claimed.

source.place: 23.22, printed p.491, using the big-cell construction 21.84, printed p.451; correction of the displayed rank-one equality to density.

proof.text: Let $Z=\overline C$ with its reduced closed structure. Left multiplication by $V$ and by $S$ preserves $Z$, since it preserves $C$. We prove by induction on $n$ that $P_\alpha^+P_{\beta_1}^-\cdots P_{\beta_n}^-\subseteq Z$. The base $n=0$ lies in $U\subset C$. If $\alpha\ne\beta_1$, commute the first two factors using [lem-sfb-simple-root-generation-mixed-commutation], then use the induction hypothesis and left $V$-stability. If $\alpha=\beta_1$, the first pair lies in $H_\alpha$. On its dense cell from step 5, a product with the remaining $n-1$ negative factors has the form $v s u P_{\beta_2}^-\cdots P_{\beta_n}^-$ with $v\in P_\alpha^-$, $s\in S$, $u\in P_\alpha^+$; induction and left $V,S$-stability put this in $Z$. Taking the closure in the $H_\alpha$ factor proves the assertion for the entire first pair. The word-kernel description of generated groups in [lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup] says the negative words are schematically dense in $V$, so $P_\alpha^+V\subseteq Z$. Right $U$-stability of $Z$ and the normalization by $S$ now give $P_\alpha^+C\subseteq Z$, hence $P_\alpha^+Z\subseteq Z$ by continuity. Thus all generators $S,P_\alpha^\pm$ preserve $Z$ on the left. Starting at the identity, every word lies in $Z$, and the same word-kernel construction gives $Z=L$. Since $C$ is locally closed and dense in $L$, it is open in $L$.

source.place: 23.22, printed p.491: induction (149), written with the dense rank-one cell and closures instead of the incorrect cell equality.

proof.text: Let $J=C_L(S)$. It is smooth and connected by [lem-sfb-torus-centralizer-smooth-connected]. If a point of $C=VSU$ centralizes $S$, its first projection centralizes $T_1$ and its second centralizes $T_0$: the latter follows from faithful flatness of $h$, by checking the commuting equations after a faithfully flat extension lifting a given torus point. Both centralizers equal the corresponding tori by [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer]. Uniqueness of the two ambient $U_i^-T_iU_i^+$ coordinates in step 5 then forces its $V$ and $U$ coordinates to be the identity. This argument holds over every algebra, so $J\cap C=S$ scheme-theoretically. Since $C$ is open, $S$ is open in $J$; it is also closed. Connectedness gives $J=S$. Every torus containing $S$ is commutative and hence lies in $J$, so $S$ is maximal; it is split since $a:S\to T_1$ is the graph isomorphism.

Apply [lem-sfb-torus-simple-root-isomorphism-criterion] to $p_1:L\to G_1$, $S$ and $T_1$. Reductivity and surjectivity were proved in step 3, maximality in step 7, and $p_1|_S=a$ is an isomorphism. The required lifts are exactly $P_\alpha^\pm$, whose first projections are isomorphisms onto $U_{\pm\alpha}$; their normalized torus-action formulas with characters $a^*(\pm\alpha)$ were checked in step 4 using [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations]. Therefore $p_1$ is an isomorphism of group schemes. This invocation controls infinitesimal kernels, not just rational points.

source.place: 23.24 and final paragraph completing 23.18, printed p.492.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-isogeny-root-power-laws] to the isomorphism $p_1$ and its inverse. For corresponding root subgroups the exponents in the two directions multiply to $1$: composing the displayed formulas on $\mathbf G_a$ gives a nonzero scalar times $x^{ee'}=x$ as a polynomial over $F$. Hence $e=e'=1$. The root and coroot identities in that node become $a^*(\alpha)=\alpha_L$ and $a\circ\alpha_L^\vee=\alpha^\vee$. Thus $a^*$ and its dual identify the full lattices, pairing, roots and coroots. The integer expansions of roots in the base $\Delta_1$ are unchanged by this lattice isomorphism, so $a^*(\Delta_1)$ is a simple-root base. Finally $p_1^{-1}(U_{\pm\alpha})=P_\alpha^\pm$, since the latter already map isomorphically onto those groups and $p_1$ is an isomorphism. These are the corresponding root subgroups, proving all remaining clauses.

source.place: 23.5, printed pp.485--486, applied to the isomorphism completing 23.18 on printed p.492.
